title: Annotator Identity Redaction and Privacy Protocol
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood's standard protocol for redacting and managing annotator identity and other sensitive metadata in probe and annotation pipelines used by the Applied ML & Evals teams. It covers the threat model, deterministic and probabilistic redaction rules, the end-to-end annotation lifecycle changes required, integration points with ProbeFarm and the Evaluator harness, monitoring and audit evidence requirements, and a staged rollout checklist.

Goals
- Eliminate storage and transit of direct identifiers for annotators (names, internal IDs mapped to payroll, email addresses) in datasets that are accessible outside the annotation service boundary.
- Maintain auditability and non-repudiation for operational and compliance review without revealing PII.
- Provide deterministic redaction heuristics that are reproducible and testable across environments (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Ensure annotation quality and productivity SLAs remain within acceptable bounds after redaction.

Scope and Definitions
- Annotator identity: any information that can be used to identify a specific human annotator (full name, corporate email, employee id).
- Annotator handle: anonymized persistent identifier assigned by the annotation service (example: ANNO::sha256(seed||region||role)).
- Probe record: the unit of work sent to annotators via ProbeFarm or the external vendor integration.
- Sensitive metadata: annotator identity, free-text comments containing PII, timestamps with sub-second precision tied to single-annotator sequences.

Threat Model
- Accidental exposure from dataset exports, debug logs, or telemetry pipelines.
- Malicious insider access to dataset stores containing raw annotation logs.
- Cross-tenant leakage in shadow evals or federated probe federations.

Redaction Principles
1) Minimize: only retain fields strictly necessary for evaluation and QA.
2) Transform: replace direct identifiers with deterministic, irreversible handles.
3) Separate: keep raw mapping (annotator handle -> identities) inside a restricted key-value store (KMS-protected, audited) with TTL and strict RBAC.
4) Audit: emit immutable audit events when mapping lookups occur; store audit records in the compliance bucket.
5) Fail-safe: pipeline components must be able to redact on-write and redact-on-read where necessary.

Redaction Rules (canonical)
- annotator_name -> REMOVE (never stored in evaluation datasets).
- annotator_email -> REMOVE.
- annotator_employee_id -> hash_sha256(lowercase(employee_id||salt)) stored as annotator_handle.
- annotator_handle: formatted as "ANNO::<first-8-hex-of-hash>". Always produced from a key derivation using a per-environment salt (salt stored in KMS).
- annotations.free_text: run PII detector; redact detected PII spans. Keep redaction markup consistent: [REDACTED:PII_EMAIL], [REDACTED:PII_PHONE], [REDACTED:PII_NAME].
- timestamps: round to nearest minute for exported datasets unless subsampled for temporal QA.

Example: redaction transformation pseudocode

1) input_record = {
  "probe_id": "pf-12345",
  "annotator_name": "Jordan Lee",
  "annotator_email": "jordan.lee@redwood.ai",
  "employee_id": "E-09876",
  "annotation": "Customer shared SSN 123-45-6789 and email alt@example.com"
}

2) salt = load_kms_secret("annotator-handle-salt")
3) handle_hash = sha256(lowercase(employee_id)+salt)
4) annotator_handle = "ANNO::" + handle_hash[0:8]
5) annotation_text = pii_detector(annotation); // returns redacted text with tags
6) output_record = {
  "probe_id": "pf-12345",
  "annotator_handle": annotator_handle,
  "annotation": annotation_text,
  "timestamp_min_rounded": "2026-02-10T15:34:00Z"
}

Operational Requirements
- Annotation service (ProbeFarm) must support redaction-on-write at the source connector for all internal and vendor systems.
- Exported evaluation bundles to S3/Blob must never contain annotator names or emails. Export job will run a post-export scanner with a zero-tolerance policy; any match blocks the export and alerts compliance.
- The raw mapping (annotator_handle -> real_identity) is stored in a dedicated vault: secret path /platform/annotations/annotator-mapper, accessible only by the Annotation Ops role and Security for incident investigation. Access is recorded with an immutable audit log (audit-entries stored in log-svc with retention 7 years).

Retention and Access Table
| Artifact | Location | Max Retention | Access Policy | Notes |
| ProbeFarm raw logs (with PII) | vaulted-store (ACM-backed) | 90 days | Annotation-Ops, Security (requires JIT approval) | used only for dispute resolution |
| Annotated dataset exports | eval-archives S3 (redacted) | 5 years | Engineering, Applied ML, Compliance | export scanned for PII before write |
| Annotator mapping table | KMS-protected vault | 30 days | Annotation-Ops (just-in-time) | rotated salt on 30-day cycle |

Integration and Tooling
- PII Detector: service name pii-detect-v2. Use model version v2025-12 with tuned thresholds: email/phone detection at 0.95 precision, names at 0.9 precision for redaction purpose. False positive handling: annotate redact spans plus keep canonical evidence for QA in the raw vault only.
- CLI Example: redaction check before export

# run a local redaction check on a dataset
redwood-evalctl redact-check --input s3://eval-bucket/staging/round-17.ndjson --rules annotator --scan-depth 3 --output ./scan-report.json

- Export hook (example YAML)
export:
  source: probefarm://round-17
  transform: redaction-on-write
  ruleset: annotator-privacy-v1
  post_scan: true
  scan_action: block-on-detect

Annotation Workflow Changes (numbered)
1) Submission: probe -> ProbeFarm -> Anonymizer module (redact-on-write).
2) Work assignment: annotator receives task with annotator_handle visible; no name/email present.
3) Free-text comments: annotator UI provides auto-suggest redaction and warns against entering PII.
4) Completed annotations: saved to evaluation datastore with redaction markers.
5) QA and adjudication: adjudicators access redacted records. If identity is required for remediation, use the private accessor flow (JIT approval).

Owner and Roles
- Annotation-Ops (owner): implements and maintains the redaction runtime and the mapping vault. Service owner: Annotation-Ops team (pager: #annotation-ops).
- Applied ML (consumer): uses redacted exports for evals and reports regressions.
- Security & Compliance: periodic audits, approves JIT access.
- Vendor-Integrations: vendors must implement matching redaction transforms before sending back datasets; vendors without capability are blocked.

Rollout Plan and Validation
- Canary (Week 0–1): enable redaction-on-write for 5% of live probe volume; monitor annotation throughput and QA delta.
- Pilot (Week 2–4): expand to 25% with escrowed raw logs in vault; run monthly compliance test: attempt export and verify block behaviour.
- Full rollout (Week 5–8): 100% redaction-on-write; rotate salt; decommission any caches that expose PII.

Success Metrics (targets)
- Export-block incidents due to PII: 0 after pilot.
- Annotation throughput delta due to UI redaction suggestions: <= 3% regression.
- QA disagreement rate between redacted and raw adjudication: <= 1.5% increase.
- JIT mapping lookups: all require approval and produce audit record; mean time to approve < 4 hours.

Monitoring and Alerting
- Alert if redaction scanner finds a direct identifier in exported dataset (severity: P1).
- Telemetry: track percent of annotations containing redaction tags, per-model and per-prompt slice. Unexpected spikes (>=5x baseline) trigger investigation.
- Daily compliance report: counts of mapping lookups, number of blocked exports, list of probes affected.

Testing and E2E Validation
- Unit tests: redaction ruleset must include positive/negative tests for 200 synthetic examples per PII class.
- Integration tests: nightly job that generates synthetic probes with seeded PII and verifies the pipeline redacts and blocks exports.
- Shadow run: run redaction module in shadow for private deployments and compare outputs to host redaction behaviour; metric: deterministic handle equality.

Appendix: Example redacted NDJSON record
{
  "probe_id": "pf-20260210-0001",
  "annotator_handle": "ANNO::4d2f9a1b",
  "annotation": "Customer reported [REDACTED:PII_SSN] in notes and alternate contact [REDACTED:PII_EMAIL]",
  "timestamp_min_rounded": "2026-02-10T15:34:00Z",
  "redaction_tags": ["PII_SSN","PII_EMAIL"]
}
